name: Next.js
subtitle: React meta-framework
creator: ZEIT (now Vercel), founded by Guillermo Rauch
description: A framework on top of React that adds file-based routing, server-side rendering, static generation, API endpoints and Server Actions, plus built-in image and font optimization. It lets you build a whole web app, front end and a light back end, in one React codebase.

languages.written: TypeScript and JavaScript, with Rust for Turbopack and SWC

concepts.explanation: Folders under app/ become routes with page.tsx and layout.tsx.
Add "use client" only where you need interactivity.
SSR, static generation, incremental regeneration and partial prerendering.
Explicit caching with the use cache directive (v16).
route.ts files that act as API endpoints.
Server functions called directly from forms.
Request interception; replaced middleware.ts in v16.

codeSamples.label: TSX · app/posts/page.tsx

pairsWith.reason: Zero-config deploys from the same team
Via Neon or Supabase on serverless hosts
Open-source auth that runs in your app

pros: First-class on Vercel, and v16 adds a Build Adapters API for other hosts
cons: Complex mental model: server vs client components and caching layers
Some features work best on Vercel, so self-hosting takes more work
Satisfaction fell from 68% to 55% in State of JS 2025

pricing.summary: Free and open source. Hosting costs depend on where you deploy.

surveys.source: Stack Overflow Developer Survey 2025, all respondents
